samples.summary: The new `command:` attribution passed by the five orchestrator actions (`docs import`, `notes import`, `slides import`, `files upload`, `files download`) is never exercised through commander — nothing fails if an action stops passing `commandPath(this)`
samples.evidence: The diff adds `command: commandPath(this)` in docs.ts:356, notes.ts:249, slides.ts:249, files.ts:46 and files.ts:71. Every test of those flows calls the orchestrators directly with hand-written args (packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:685-770 `runDocsImport({file:'a.docx', replace:'doc-1', yes:true}, …)`, docs-import.test.ts, notes-import.test.ts, slides-import.test.ts, files-*.test.ts) and never supplies or asserts `command`. `errorEnvelope`/`upstreamErrorJson` are tested with a literal string ('docs.import' in output.test.ts:356) rather than through the action. The repo's own comment at upstream-error.test.ts:187-190 states the standard being missed here: "Asserting on the helper alone cannot catch a site that stops calling it". Dropping `command` from any of those five actions leaves the whole CLI suite green.
searchedFor: grep 'docs\.import|notes\.import|slides\.import|files\.upload|files\.download' in packages/cli/test (only schema.test.ts and output.test.ts literals)

samples.summary: `announceLoginUrl`'s owner-only file mode (0o600, plus the rmSync-before-write that stops an existing world-readable file keeping its permissions) is asserted nowhere
samples.evidence: login.ts:151-163 writes the login URL with `{ mode: 0o600 }` and claims '(readable only by you)'. packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts only asserts the file's path is announced and its contents match (`readFileSync(urlPath,'utf-8')`) and that it is removed afterwards; no `statSync(...).mode` check. The repo does test this property elsewhere (packages/cli/test/session.test.ts:70-75), so the omission is a gap rather than a convention.

samples.summary: The TTY branch of `announceLoginUrl` (prints the secret-bearing URL to stderr) has no test; the helper is neither exported nor injectable, so only the non-TTY branch is reachable under vitest
samples.evidence: login.ts:141-172 has three branches: stderr-is-a-TTY (prints the URL), non-TTY (writes the 0600 file), and write-failure (prints the 'not printed' advice). `announceLoginUrl` is module-private and reads `process.stderr.isTTY` directly, unlike the import orchestrators which take `isTTY` through their IO seam (src/docs/import.ts:45). All new tests (login-callback.test.ts, login.test.ts:404) run with a non-TTY stderr, so the printing branch and the catch branch are untested.

samples.summary: Two cookie-policy tests iterate `res.cookie.mock.calls` with no call-count guard, so they pass vacuously if the refresh path stops setting cookies at all
samples.evidence: auth.controller.spec.ts:556-568 ('sets SameSite=Lax with secure=false outside production') and :570-584 ('never sets SameSite=None on auth cookies') only loop over the recorded calls; with zero calls both loop bodies are skipped and the tests pass. Its production sibling at :540 does assert `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)`, showing the guard was deliberate there and simply absent here.

samples.summary: The five-minute timeout test's key assertion mirrors the source constant, and the fake-timer part does not pin the boundary
samples.evidence: `expect(CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS).toBe(5 * 60 * 1000)` is a restatement of the literal in login.ts:481, so editing both keeps it green; the comment claims the CLI and the backend's `CLI_STATE_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_MS` 'must agree' but nothing compares the two (they live in different packages and no cross-check exists). The timer half advances 60_000 then a further CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS (360s total), so any timeout in (60s, 360s] would also pass — the 'waits out the whole five-minute window' claim is not actually pinned.
searchedFor: grep CLI_STATE_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_MS in packages/backend and packages/cli

samples.summary: No test asserts that a bare copy of the confirm cookie is now refused as `?confirm=` — the exact regression the HMAC token introduces
samples.evidence: The diff replaces the old `{ confirm: 'secret-value' }` positive case with `cliConfirmToken(...)`. The remaining negative cases replay a *valid token* against another port/challenge (spec lines ~131-166). A middleware that kept `timingSafeEqualStr(confirm, cookie)` as an additional accepted path would fail none of the new tests except indirectly. Also untested: the length-prefixing claim in cliConfirmToken's doc ('"9|87,6" vs "98|7,6"') — no test constructs the re-cut collision it exists to prevent.

samples.summary: The only wiring of `logSafeUrl` — the pino `req` serializer — has no test; `logSafeUrl` itself is well covered but nothing proves the access log uses it
samples.evidence: app.module.ts:70 changes `url: req.url` to `url: logSafeUrl(req.url)`. `grep logSafeUrl` finds only log-safe-url.ts, its spec, and app.module.ts; there is no app.module spec and no e2e assertion over the emitted log line, so reverting the serializer line leaves the backend suite green.

samples.summary: The oversized-envelope fallback in `safeEnvelope` is never exercised with a `command`, so the newly added `...(command ? { command } : {})` in that branch is uncovered
samples.evidence: upstream-error.test.ts:151-162 ('drops sibling fields once the envelope stops being small') calls `forwardUpstreamError` with no `command` argument, and the new output.test.ts `upstreamErrorJson` cases all use small bodies. Dropping `command` from the clamped branch would keep every test green — precisely the attribution loss the change exists to prevent, on the path where an agent most needs it.

samples.summary: Env hygiene is applied to `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` but not `COOKIE_SECURE`, which `useSecureCookies()` reads first — the same fragility the diff's own comments set out to fix
samples.evidence: github-auth.guard.spec.ts:88-92 clears both variables; the cli-login-confirm spec's `run` helper (lines 19-35) and auth.controller.spec.ts's new describes (lines 495-497, 603-605) clear only `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL`. Since isSecureCookie() (oauth-state.ts:229-232) consults `COOKIE_SECURE` before the callback URL, an ambient `COOKIE_SECURE` decides these assertions instead of the case under test — e.g. the 'shows no confirmation page where the cookie is plantable' case (spec ~line 195) would silently exercise the opposite branch with `COOKIE_SECURE=true`.
searchedFor: read the three new backend spec describes' beforeEach/afterEach blocks

finding.summary: The new `command:` attribution passed by the five orchestrator actions (`docs import`, `notes import`, `slides import`, `files upload`, `files download`) is never exercised through commander — nothing fails if an action stops passing `commandPath(this)`
finding.evidence: The diff adds `command: commandPath(this)` in docs.ts:356, notes.ts:249, slides.ts:249, files.ts:46 and files.ts:71. Every test of those flows calls the orchestrators directly with hand-written args (packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:685-770 `runDocsImport({file:'a.docx', replace:'doc-1', yes:true}, …)`, docs-import.test.ts, notes-import.test.ts, slides-import.test.ts, files-*.test.ts) and never supplies or asserts `command`. `errorEnvelope`/`upstreamErrorJson` are tested with a literal string ('docs.import' in output.test.ts:356) rather than through the action. The repo's own comment at upstream-error.test.ts:187-190 states the standard being missed here: "Asserting on the helper alone cannot catch a site that stops calling it". Dropping `command` from any of those five actions leaves the whole CLI suite green.
searchedFor: grep 'docs\.import|notes\.import|slides\.import|files\.upload|files\.download' in packages/cli/test (only schema.test.ts and output.test.ts literals)

verdict.reason: The five actions do pass `command: commandPath(this)` (docs.ts:356, notes.ts:249, slides.ts:249, files.ts:46, files.ts:76) and the field is optional in every orchestrator arg type (docs/import.ts:101, files/upload.ts:124), so dropping it breaks neither the build nor any test. Every commander-driven attribution suite excludes these commands: upstream-error.test.ts:267-341 builds a real program and asserts `command` for ~40 argv cases, but its CASES list contains no docs/notes/slides import, no files upload, no files download; output.test.ts:605-739 covers docs.get / sheets.cells.get / docs.content / schema; ctx.test.ts:140 covers ctx.switch; command-exit-codes.test.ts:73-128 drives only content/export/get/list. The one suite that does cover the five (upstream-error.test.ts:638-889) calls the orchestrators directly with hand-written args (691-869) and its assertions (877-886) expect envelopes with no `command` key at all. Repo-wide grep of runDocsImport/runNotesImport/runSlidesImport/runFilesUpload/runFilesDownload finds no other test invocation, no vi.mock of those modules, no occurrence of `command` anywhere in docs-import/notes-import/slides-import/files-upload/files-download/slides-pptx-import tests, and no test that spawns the CLI binary. files-format.test.ts and namespaces.test.ts drive `files` through commander but only for rename/delete/list/get and name registration. So the new attribution on these five paths has no test that can fail if an action stops passing it - a real missing-test gap by the repo's own stated standard at upstream-error.test.ts:187-190.

mergedFrom.summary: No test pins the warning's interaction with an explicit COOKIE_SECURE=false on a production non-loopback http origin

finding.summary: No test covers that COOKIE_SECURE now decides `cliLoginAvailable` — the CLI consent gate on a plain-http, non-loopback origin
finding.evidence: `cliLoginAvailable` (github-auth.guard.ts:215) is `secureCookies(...) || loopbackCallback(...)`, so the new `COOKIE_SECURE` short-circuit in `secureCookies` (line 159-160) newly makes a CLI login startable on a plain-http non-loopback origin (COOKIE_SECURE=true) and newly *refuses* one on an https origin (COOKIE_SECURE=false). The existing gate tests use only `insecureConfig()`/`httpsConfig()` (spec lines 444-466, 686-700); the three new COOKIE_SECURE tests assert only `secureCookies()`'s return, `loginCookieName`, and the web state cookie's `secure` option. Nothing exercises `canActivate` with a CLI query under an overridden config, so a regression in either direction of that gate would pass green.

verdict.reason: The alleged missing coverage exists. `github-auth.guard.spec.ts` has `describe('CLI login availability')` (lines 319-357) nested in `describe('GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate')`, which runs the real guard's `canActivate` with a CLI query under an overridden `COOKIE_SECURE` in both directions: line 330-339 sets a plain-http non-loopback `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` plus `COOKIE_SECURE=true` and asserts the start succeeds (`result === true`, `createState` called); line 341-349 sets an https callback plus `COOKIE_SECURE=false` and asserts the 400 refusal `/Command-line sign-in requires an https server/`. Lines 320-328 and 351-356 pin the un-overridden baselines. The `activate` helper (100-111) constructs the real `GitHubAuthGuard` and stubs only the passport super `canActivate` (line 92), so `assertCliLoginAvailable` -> `cliLoginAvailable()` -> `useSecureCookies()` (github-auth.guard.ts:72-75, 232-244) executes for real against env cleared per test (88-98). A regression in either direction of the gate would therefore fail, contradicting the finding's core claim. The finding's quoted line numbers (guard:215, spec 444-466/686-700) do not match this repository's files.
